witnesses.provenance: Solana's per-transaction MAX_COMPUTE_UNIT_LIMIT is 1,400,000 compute units. It is the chain's limit, not ours, and the ProgramTest ceiling this campaign runs under is set to exactly it and never raised.

A null `wire_bytes` is the emitter's word for 'did not measure', which is honest but is not a claim that the frame fits. It matters more than usual here, because the next witness is where the campaign's real packet position is written down.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.label | startswith("retirement checkpoint:")) | "\(.label | split(": ")[1] | split(" ")[0])=\(.wire_bytes)"] | unique | sort | join(" + ")
witnesses.provenance: All twelve were 2,005 to 2,157 bytes as legacy messages against Solana's 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES -- up to 925 over -- so not one of them could be submitted anywhere, and ProgramTest submits no packet to say so. The aggregate retirement had ALREADY been split into four transactions to get this far; the split alone does not reach the packet, and the table is what carries it. They now execute as v0 messages over ONE table frozen for the chain: the four 35-meta frames share their coordinates, so a table per route would be a rent per route for a single market's retirement. 34 of the 35 addresses become one-byte indexes and two stay static -- the payer and the invoked program, which no table can move. The two `finish` figures differ by one byte because the substituted-wallet hostile collapses two coordinates onto one address and so resolves 33 rather than 34. These are DATA-bound frames now: the requests are 744 to 864 bytes and no table touches those, so there is no third lever if a request grows. Figures here exclude the ComputeBudget instructions; AGGREGATE_RETIREMENT_CHECKPOINT_SPLIT_2026_08_28.md records 1,135/1,191/1,191/1,071, which is these numbers plus the 52 bytes of a compute-unit limit and a priority fee.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select(.error != null) | select([.logs[] | select(contains("custom program error: 0x"))] | length == 0)] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: The Solana runtime reports a privilege, frame or account refusal it decides ITSELF as a bare InstructionError with no `custom program error:` log line; that line appears only when a program returned ProgramError::Custom. Every one of this campaign's eight refusals is a decision Core or Claims made on a named field, so a bare runtime refusal appearing here would mean a hostile case stopped being about the retirement chain.

CHECKPOINT_RETIREMENT_* declares four instruction shapes -- prepare, close-vault, close-replay, finish -- and `build_checkpoint_market_retirement_v1` returns exactly those four. A fifth accepted transaction would mean the campaign found a second way into the terminal state; a fourth becoming a third would mean a stage stopped being reachable.

witnesses.query: [.transactions[] | select([.logs[] | select(test("^Program 8yRstXxCnC3jTgWtUFVRLJ51ojpkUW1kw9eRsrHhAK4R invoke"))] | length > 0) | .label] | length | tostring
witnesses.provenance: Claims is handed off exactly once, by the prepare. Only two of the twelve transactions may reach the Claims program at all -- the accepted prepare and the hostile whose aggregate owner was substituted -- and in particular the REPLAYED prepare must not, because a replay that re-entered the handoff would be spending Claims compute to discover a fact Core already holds in its own checkpoint. The address is this tier's gauntlet-local Claims id from programs.json.

Against Solana's 1,232-byte PACKET_DATA_BYTES. Twelve transactions were over it before 2026-09-02, which is what the earlier form of this witness recorded as a defect. Nulls are excluded on purpose: an unmeasured transaction is not a transaction that fits, and `retirement-checkpoint-measured-every-transaction` is what holds that count at zero.
